name: Prone press-up (McKenzie)
summary: Face down, hands under the shoulders, press the upper body up while the hips stay on the floor.
setup: Lie on your front, side-on to the phone at floor level, hands under the shoulders. Press the arms straight to lift the chest, letting the back sag and the hips stay down. Lower slowly.
brief: Lie on your front, hands under the shoulders. Press the arms straight to lift the chest, letting the back sag and the hips stay down.
why: From the side the shoulder–hip line tilts up from the floor each press, so reps are counted. The hips lifting — the one fault that matters — is behind the arms from most angles.
tempo: Up 2 s, hold 2 s, down 2 s.
dosage: 10 reps, every 2 hours in a flare.
progression: Lock the elbows fully; hold the top longer.
contraindications: Pain moving further down the leg on the press — stop and tell your physio.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Hips lifting off the floor
faults.cue: Keep the hips on the floor
faults.tip: Let the pelvis hang heavy; if the hips lift, the arms are doing a push-up instead of an extension.

faults.label: Pain moving down the leg
faults.tip: Pain travelling further from the back is the one signal to stop and tell your physio. Pain moving toward the back is a good sign.

faults.label: Tensing the back muscles
faults.tip: The arms lift you; the back muscles stay soft so the joints can move.

faults.label: Squeezing the buttocks
faults.tip: Clenching the glutes tips the pelvis and blocks the extension you are trying to get.

guide.stop: Pain spreading further down the leg.
guide.cannotSee: The hips lifting, and whether the back is relaxed.
